issues.description: flattenRef now has two distinct dedup passes whose loop invariants are not stated and overlap subtly
issues.detail: The function first merges ref, restores _cached, then strips parent-only keys, then JSON.stringify-dedupes against refSeen.def, then again against parentSeen.def. Each pass needs an invariant: 'after this block, schema contains exactly the properties that differ from X'. Without those stated, future maintainers cannot tell whether the parent-extracted dedup and the ref-extracted dedup can both fire and double-strip.

issues.description: JSON.stringify used as a structural equality test inside hot dedup loops is both asymptotically and practically fragile
issues.detail: Comparing schema[key] to refSeen.def![key] via JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b) is O(size of value) per key, runs once per key per seen entry, and silently disagrees for objects with reordered keys or undefined values. For a converter that may process large nested schemas this is ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW and semantically wrong on key-order edge cases. A small deepEqual helper would be both faster and correct.

issues.description: Termination of flattenRef relies on a single sentinel and recurses through both seen.ref and seen.parent without a shared visited set
issues.detail: seen.ref = null guards the ref chain, but the new seen.parent branch calls flattenRef(seen.parent) before any guard on parent. If a parent's own ref later loops back through this node, the only thing stopping infinite recursion is that seen.ref was nulled on the first entry. A second sentinel (seen.parent visited) or an explicit termination argument would make this provable rather than incidental.

issues.description: overrideCount jumping from 6 to 12 is asserted but not explained
issues.detail: The test 'override: do not run on references' updated its expectation from 6 to 12 with no comment. That is exactly the kind of silent doubling a future reader needs the invariant for: is override now correctly running once per (schema, context) where before it was suppressed on parents, or is it double-firing? A one-line literate comment in the test stating the new invariant would prevent a regression masquerading as an intentional change.

issues.description: play.ts committed as a scratch debugging script with a path-relative import
issues.detail: play.ts now imports from './packages/zod/src/index.js' and console.logs two cases. This is a debugging artifact, not a literate example; it will rot and confuse readers who treat top-level files as canonical. Either delete it before merge or convert it into a documented example with the invariant under test stated in a comment.

issues.description: The new ref/parent distinction in Seen deserves a literate comment block, not just two one-liners
issues.detail: The whole PR hinges on separating 'ref = schema to inherit JSON properties from' from 'parent = clone-chain parent for $ref propagation'. The inline doc comments are accurate but terse. A short paragraph above the interface explaining the two roles, when each is set, and how flattenRef consumes them would make this code readable in the Knuth sense and reduce the chance the next contributor collapses them again.

review.summary: The change correctly separates two previously conflated concepts in Seen (ref for property inheritance, parent for clone-chain $ref propagation), and the new test for readonly().meta({id}).describe() captures a real bug fix. However, flattenRef has grown into a multi-pass mutator whose loop invariants are not stated, and it leans on JSON.stringify as a structural-equality oracle in dedup loops — that is both ASYMPTOTICALLY-OK-PRACTICALLY-SLOW and semantically brittle. Termination across the new parent recursion is incidental rather than proven; a second sentinel would make it auditable. The test assertion change from 6 to 12 overrides should be annotated with the new invariant, and play.ts should not ship as a scratch script. Overall verdict: UNDER-AUDITED — the fix appears correct but the literate-programming-grade explanation and complexity audit are missing.
